request.spec:
A claim now has a status. It starts as DRAFT; it can be opened (OPEN) and then settled
(SETTLED); a DRAFT or OPEN claim can be voided (VOID). A SETTLED or VOID claim cannot change
status, and the buttons for a change that is not allowed are refused with an error on the claim.
Only OPEN and SETTLED claims count toward claimed, due-total and every total; drafts and voided
claims do not. Show each claim's status. Every status change writes an audit line: CLAIM_OPENED,
CLAIM_SETTLED or CLAIM_VOIDED, each with person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A claim now has a status. It starts as DRAFT; it can be opened (OPEN) and then settled
(SETTLED); a DRAFT or OPEN claim can be voided (VOID). A SETTLED or VOID claim cannot change
status, and the buttons for a change that is not allowed are refused with an error on the claim.
Only OPEN and SETTLED claims count toward claimed, due-total and every total; drafts and voided
claims do not. Show each claim's status. Every status change writes an audit line: CLAIM_OPENED,
CLAIM_SETTLED or CLAIM_VOIDED, each with person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims now have a status, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

**Stored data**
- A new migration, `V7__claim_status.sql`, adds a `status` column to claims. It defaults to `DRAFT`, so claims that already exist start as drafts.

**Server**
- A new `ClaimStatus` enum holds the rules: DRAFT can go to OPEN, OPEN to SETTLED, and DRAFT or OPEN to VOID. SETTLED and VOID can't change.
- There are three new endpoints, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{id}/open`, `/settle` and `/void`. A change the rules don't allow is refused with a 409 and writes nothing.
- A successful change writes `CLAIM_OPENED`, `CLAIM_SETTLED` or `CLAIM_VOIDED` to the audit file in the same form as the other claim lines (`… person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>`).
- The status is now part of the claim the API returns.

**Front end** (`claims.ts`)
- Each claim row shows its status (`claim-status`) and has Open, Settle and Void buttons (`claim-open`, `claim-settle`, `claim-void`).
- A refused change shows an error on that claim (`claim-error`). It clears when you next act on that row or press Edit.
- Only OPEN and SETTLED claims count toward claimed, due-total and the sheet totals. All the totals use one shared sum, so they all apply this rule.

Two behaviours you might not expect, both because the test requires them:
- All three buttons show for every claim, even when the change isn't allowed. Pressing one that isn't allowed shows the error rather than the button being hidden.
- A claim's own Due column still shows its amount times the rate, even for draft and voided claims; only the totals leave those claims out.

Editing a claim is still allowed whatever its status; the change request didn't restrict it.
